la:verb:diiudico.html:
dī-jūdĭco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
With the idea of the verb predominating, to judge by discerning or distinguishing; to decide, determine (class.).
Prop.: ego dicam, quod mihi in mentem venit: tu dijudica,; so absol., : aliena melius quam sua,: callide verbis controversias, non aequitate,; so, controversiam,: causam,: litem, et saep.—With acc. and inf.: quam (sc. uxorem) omnium Thebis vir unam esse optimam dijudicat,judges, accounts,.—With rel. clause: neque dijudicari posset, uter utri virtute anteferendus videretur, al.—
Transf., to decide by arms: dijudicatā belli fortunā,: discordiae civium ferro,.—
With the idea of the particle predominating, to discern by judging; to distinguish (between two): vera et falsa,; cf.: recta ac prava,: jus et injuriam, honesta ac turpia (shortly before: legem bonam a mala dividere),: amorem verum et fictum,: benevolum et simulatorem,; also: vera a falsis, veri similia ab incredibilibus (with distinguere),: inter has sententias,; for which simply: sententias subtilissime,.—With rel. clause: dijudicandum est, immodicum sit an grande,.

la:verb:diiungo.gloss: to disjoin, disunite, separate, part, divide
